text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 28th in history:
1491 - King Henry VIII was born in Greenwich, London, the second son of Henry VII. He married six times but ended up beheading two of them.
1519 - Charles I of Spain became Holy Roman Emperor and ruled until 1556 as Charles V.
1577 - Sir Peter Paul Rubens, Flemish artist and one of the most renowned painters of his time, born.
1629 - The Peace of Alais ended the Huguenot revolt in France.
1712 - Jean Jacques Rousseau, French philosopher whose works influenced the revolution, born in Geneva.
1776 - During the American Revolution, the British were defeated at the first Battle of Charleston; on the same day in 1778, the British thwarted an American attack at the Battle of Monmouth.
1836 - James Madison, fourth U.S. president (1809-17), died.
1838 - The coronation of Queen Victoria took place in Westminster Abbey, a year after she had ascended the throne.
1861 - Robert (O'Hara) Burke, Irish-born Australian explorer who crossed Australia from south to north, died on the return journey.
1867 - Luigi Pirandello, Italian playwright and Nobel Prize winner, born; best remembered for his "Six Characters in Search of an Author" first performed in 1921.
1873 - Alexis Carrel, French-born U.S. surgeon and Nobel Prize winner, born. His work later played an important part in tissue transplants.
1883 - Pierre Laval, French politician and prime minister, born. He was prime minister of the Vichy government in World War Two; he was tried for treason and shot after the war ended.
1902 - Richard Rodgers, American composer and half of the Rodgers and Hammerstein and Rodgers and Hart partnerships, born.
1902 - The U.S. bought the concession to build a Panama canal from a French company for 40 million dollars.
1914 - A Serbian nationalist assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand, the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, and his wife in Sarajevo; the incident was widely held to have sparked World War One.
1919 - The end of World War One was marked by the signing of the Treaty of Versailles between Germany and the allies.
1926 - Mel Brooks, U.S. actor, writer, producer and director, notably of "The Producers", "Blazing Saddles" and "High Anxiety", born as Melvin Kaminsky.
1935 - U.S. President Roosevelt ordered a federal gold vault to be built at Fort Knox, Kentucky.
1940 - Soviet troops occupied the Romanian regions of Bessarabia and Bucovina.
1948 - The Yugoslav Communist Party was expelled from COMINFORM at a meeting in Bucharest. It marked the formal breach in relations between Yugoslavia and the rest of the Communist bloc.
1950 - In one of the biggest soccer upsets ever, England were beaten 1-0 by the United States in a World Cup match in Brazil.
1950 - North Korean troops captured Seoul.
1970 - U.S. troops began their withdrawal from Cambodia.
1976 - The Indian Ocean islands of Seychelles became an independent republic within the Commonwealth after 160 years of British rule.
1979 - The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), meeting in Geneva, agreed on a two-tier pricing system for oil.
1981 - In Iran, 74 people, including Chief Justice Ayatollah Beheshti, were killed by a bomb attack on the headquarters of the Islamic Republican Party.
1988 - After 15 months of evidence, the trial of Spanish oil dealers accused of selling industrial rapeseed oil for human consumption, ended; the oil killed 650 and maimed 25,000.
1992 - Two earthquakes, including the third strongest in the U.S. this century at 7.4 on the Richter scale, rocked southern California.
1996 - President Suleyman Demirel approved Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan as Turkey's first Islamist prime minister in a coalition with conservative Tansu Ciller.
1996 - Russian troops began a long-promised pullout from Chechnya.
